templates.title: MCP Router
templates.description: MCP gateway beside its own Postgres: install MCP servers from registries or npm and serve them all over streamable HTTP, one endpoint each plus a merged one.
templates.note: Set BETTER_AUTH_SECRET. Open the web UI on port 3000 and sign in, then make API keys for MCP clients in Settings.

env.name: BETTER_AUTH_SECRET
env.label: Session secret
env.description: Required: signs web UI sessions. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32

env.name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
env.label: Database password
env.description: Password for the bundled Postgres, which keeps the router's config. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 16

env.name: MCP_ROUTER_PORT
env.label: Host port
env.description: Port the web UI and the MCP endpoints are published on.

env.name: MCP_ROUTER_DATA
env.label: Data folder
env.description: Host folder for installed server packages and caches (the config is in Postgres). It must be writable by uid 1000, which the container runs as.

env.name: SECURE_LOCAL_NET
env.label: Trusted network sign-in
env.description: Only on a network you trust: whoever opens the web UI is signed in as the local admin. MCP clients still need an API key, made in Settings.

select.text: No, sign in through an OIDC provider
Yes, sign in as the local admin

env.name: MCP_ROUTER_TOKEN
env.label: Old router token (optional)
env.description: Upgrading: the token your MCP clients already use. It is imported as an API key with the same value.

templates.title: MCP Router (single container)
templates.description: MCP gateway: install MCP servers from registries or npm and serve them all over streamable HTTP, one endpoint each plus a merged one. Uses a Postgres you already run.
templates.note: Needs a Postgres you already run: set DATABASE_URL to it. Set BETTER_AUTH_SECRET. Open the web UI on port 3000 and sign in, then make API keys for MCP clients in Settings.

env.name: DATABASE_URL
env.label: Postgres URL
env.description: Required: the Postgres that keeps the router's config, e.g. postgres://mcp_router:secret@192.168.1.20:5432/mcp_router. The router refuses to start without it.

env.name: BETTER_AUTH_SECRET
env.label: Session secret
env.description: Required: signs web UI sessions. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32

env.name: SECURE_LOCAL_NET
env.label: Trusted network sign-in (true/false)
env.description: Only on a network you trust: whoever opens the web UI is signed in as the local admin. MCP clients still need an API key.

env.name: MCP_ROUTER_TOKEN
env.label: Old router token (optional)
env.description: Upgrading: the token your MCP clients already use. It is imported as an API key with the same value.
